definition: Managing the risk that a model, dataset, plugin or dependency an AI system relies on has been tampered with or compromised.
details: Modern AI applications assemble third-party models, weights, datasets, prompts and MCP tools; any of those links can carry backdoors, poisoned data or malicious code. Supply-chain controls track provenance, pin versions, scan artifacts and verify integrity before anything reaches production.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. In plain words: Managing the risk that a model, dataset, plugin or dependency an AI system relies on has been tampered with or compromised. Here is how it actually plays out: Modern AI applications assemble third-party models, weights, datasets, prompts and MCP tools; any of those links can carry backdoors, poisoned data or malicious code. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. That deliberate caution is AI Supply Chain Security.
